newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 28.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - Apr 28.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Public Relations, Brand-name Products, Consumer Trends and the Media
ADVERTISING, MARKETING & PUBLIC RELATIONS:

BONN - Health Minister Horst Seehofer has called for fewer beer and liquor advertisements during sports programming. In an interview with the Berliner Morgenpost newspaper, Seehofer asked public and private television channels voluntarily to limit alcohol advertisement to certain times and programmes. (Reuter)
HAMBURG - Hamburg-based advertising agency Jung von Matt says it has designed a nationwide campaign for the Wetterkanal, a weather channel. (Reuter)

KRONBERG - The international public relations group Pinnacle Worldwide has seven new members, its Kronberg agency says. In Europe, Menedetter PR in Austria has joined the group. The other six agencies are in the Asia-Pacific region. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Publicis has designed a new campaign for Vittel mineral water. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Advertising agency Ammirati Puris Lintas has pitched for the account of Prinz events magazine. (Horizont)
MEDIA:

HAMBURG - Media mogul Leo Kirch has apparently bought the pay TV rights to the last available MGM Studios films for several hundred million marks. Kirch secured the rights to show old and new films from the Hollywood studios for 10 years on premium cable channels or on a pay-per-view basis. (Der Spiegel)

LUXEMBOURG - Club RTL, a joint project by the Luxembourg-based CLT group and media group Bertelsmann for digital television distribution, has cost CLT 4.127 billion Luxembourg francs ($120 million), the company says. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

HAMBURG - The concentration of German beer production will continue unabated, says the chairman of Holsten beer company Wilfried Rinke. Faced with an international beer market in which fewer and fewer companies control the business, the German industry cannot continue to survive with hundreds of often very small breweries. (Reuter)

BONN - Hotel and restaurant association Dehoga says the weak German economy has lead to a trend toward fast food consumption. Dehoga president Erich Kaub says while restaurants posted 3.6 percent lower turnover in 1995, fast food chains saw a boom. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:

MUNICH - The former chairman of munitions manufacturer Krauss-Maffei AG, Burkhard Wollschlaeger, will take over as chairman of the board at troubled electronics firm Grundig, says the Donaukurier newspaper, citing "reliable sources". Current chairman Christian Schwarz-Schilling is expected to step down at the end of May. (Reuter)
DUESSELDORF - Mannesmann AG says the head of its mobile phone network, Harald Stoeber, will move over to take control of its Arcor telecommunications network. (Reuter)
FRANKFURT - Thomas Pfau took over as head of distribution for Reebok Germany at the beginning of April. (Horizont)
